summary: The prepared main source already contains the request-isolation correction described by related issue #32089, introduced by upstream PR #30177 after the affected 0.5.17 release. Full hidden-state capture now advances the packed-row offset for requests that do not themselves return hidden states and uses each request's snapshotted forwarded-row count. Added direct regression and boundary coverage; no production source change was needed.

tests.what_was_measured: All nine unit tests passed, including the mixed false/true request regression, cached-prefix/zero-forward-row boundaries, and the existing middle-chunk/full-vs-last cases.

tests.command: PYTHONPATH=python /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-1064c7fdb91d/venv/bin/python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/managers/test_batch_result_processor_hidden_states.py::TestPrefillHiddenStateOffsets::test_non_requesting_request_still_advances_full_capture_offset (with the old skip-without-advance behavior temporarily restored)
tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before proof: the packed offset was 3 instead of 8, demonstrating that the old behavior selects an earlier request's rows. The temporary source modification was reverted before final validation.
Final-source validation: three offset regression methods passed, with two full/last subcases.

On the assigned AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950, a device-resident 8-row tensor produced offset 8 and selected rows [[20], [21], [22]] for the requesting request, matching an independent literal reference.

remaining_limitations: Kimi-K3 weights were not available, so the random production symptom was not reproduced with that model.

The source report used eight NVIDIA B300 GPUs; this environment provides one AMD gfx950 GPU. No claim is made about B300, tensor parallelism, multi-node execution, Kimi-K3 semantic accuracy, or the complete serving workload.
The GPU fixture validates the identified packed hidden-state isolation mechanism only; it is not a full HTTP/model reproduction.

Issue #34259 contains no deterministic reproducer. The reporter stated that the symptom was seen on 0.5.17 but not on main, which is consistent with PR #30177 landing afterward, but does not prove that this was the only possible cause.
